title: His father the gambler and bronco breaker
summary: His father gambled heavily and would raise money by going to ranches to break horses; Durham never saw him thrown.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, Eddie, listen, tell me more about your father. Tell me about -- you said he was a drinking man. He was a gambling man, you said.
Yeah, great gambler.
He was a great gambler?
Yeah, all those fellas, they gamble all the time.
Well, you told me that if he needed some change, what would he do in the morning you said?

Well, he had one of those riding saddles, because he'd put his regular saddle on the horse and then sometime he'd use that saddle on his horse to get that -- take it off his horse. But most of the times, he -- that saddle -- he
wouldn't use that saddle to ride on the horse. That was -- He'd ride bareback?
No, he'd have another saddle he'd ride his horse with. But that was a special saddle he'd use to put on one of them other horses.
Oh.
They'd rope a horse (inaudible).
So in other words, he went out to --
-- throw a saddle on. They let you throw a saddle on them.
Oh, they will?

Some of them will. Some of them try to buck. But they tie them up, feet and all, rope him up so he can't move and they'd put a saddle on him and then (inaudible) get on it. Most of them let you put a saddle on them. Some of them don't like it, but a saddle ain't big. They don't like a man on top of them.
No. Well, listen, we didn't make it really clear. What you told me was that if he needed $25, he'd go out to what? To a ranch?
Yeah, he'd go to another ranch. He knew everybody --
And say to them?
'Mr. So and So, you got a horse I can break this morning?' 'Oh, here's Joe Durham. Yeah, yeah, the
bronco, yeah."
And show him what the horse looked like?
He'd show him the horse and (inaudible) may be two days before he could catch that horse sometime.
(Laughter.)
Oh, really?
(Inaudible) wanted that money.
(Laughter.)
He'd ride that horse down the road and (inaudible).
And would he come in riding that?
No, he wouldn't come in riding the horse. But he'd lead the horse in, huh?
He'd lead him in and bring him in the corral and ride him.
No kidding.
Lead him in, bring (inaudible).
So you said you never saw your father thrown off a horse.
Never seen him get throwed. I saw guys -- they rode at least 20 horses during one show in the --
Yeah, in the -- yeah, in the rodeos.
That was one act. For a half hour, they'd ride horse right after another. (Inaudible) 80 guys standing in line. They'd get on this horse and ride and they'd

buck. People would see that. But if the guy didn't get throwed -- most of the times, they'd throw them ten feet over. They'd throw them guys off of them horses. And you didn't get throwed off, you'd have to jump off. They'd pull him off if that horse started breaking a little bit. Most of the time they threw them off, threw the guys off of them.
Yeah, because you mean, if you stay on a horse, he's no longer a bronco.
Oh, if you ever stay on him (inaudible), he's broke.
Yeah.
See, he wouldn't be no good for the show next day.
